One-screen UI: before and after

2026-09-29 · the ten "consolidate the phone UI" items. Every picture is a real capture from the editor at the phone's own 1080 × 1920, the game camera and every UI panel rendered together (UiShots.Capture).

How to read this. Red dashed boxes on the left are what was wrong; orange boxes on the right are what changed, numbered to the notes under each pair. The frame rate reads 200 FPS in the race pictures because the editor was being stepped one fixed physics tick at a time to take them, not because of anything the game does.

The layout check, before and after

Each screen was walked element by element (UiShots.CheckLayout, re-runnable with training/tools/ui_shots.sh): anything off the screen, anything that needs a scroll, text under 26 px at the 1080 px reference, text cut off by its box, and the five corner items in their corners.

1 · The race

Before

After

  • AThe event name and the race clock were drawn underneath the game name and MENU, so the clock could not be read during a race.
  • BTwo rows of buttons: GUST / SHOVE / SLICK / AUTO, then RESTART and a STATS button that disappeared against the sky.
  • 1The top bar now starts under the frame's row. Clock readable for the whole race.
  • 2All race controls in one row, each an icon over one word, all on a dark ground so they read over sky or deck.

2 · Stats as badges

Before

After (STATS pressed)

  • 3Speed, distance, uprightness and attempt as four badges in one line, with the policy name above them. The athlete name bar now measures where the controls are and sits on top of them, instead of guessing a 352 px margin.

3 · Diagnostics: no scrolling

Before

After: the field

After: one athlete

  • DOne full card per athlete in a scroll view: eight athletes made 8,457 px to scroll through, and the sheet covered DEBUG and the version.
  • 4One line per athlete (speed, falls, uprightness, clamping, graded by colour); sixteen fit without scrolling.
  • 5The sheet stops at the frame's rows, so DEBUG (which closes it), the version, MENU and the frame rate stay on screen.

4 · Diagnostics: frame page

Before

After

  • 6Tapping the frame-rate chip opens this page directly.
  • 7New Thermal row: whether the phone is heating up and what render scale that has cost. It reads "no provider" until Adaptive Performance is switched on in Project Settings (one checkbox, see the summary).

Draw calls and triangles read 0 in both pictures: those counters only work on a device, not in a stepped editor. The triangle figures in the README were counted a different way for that reason.

Before

After

  • ETwo rows: NONE / ONE EACH / START, then CARDS and START SEASON.
  • 8One row: NONE, ONE EACH, SEASON (plus END while a season runs), and START.

6 · Athlete cards

Before

After

  • 10Tap a tile to turn it over: races, wins, podiums, falls, top speed, work done, and best mark per event. Tap again to turn it back. The counts and steppers are still one tap away.

7 · The evaluation menu, folded into SETTINGS

Before: its own screen

After: a page of DEBUG

  • 11SETTINGS is the third page of the diagnostics sheet, reachable from DEBUG on every screen.
  • 12Quality tier and frame-rate target, applied on the tap. The old screen's third control, the checkpoint picker, was read by nothing in the game, so it was dropped; the page says how many checkpoints are built in instead. The scene and its code are removed.

8 · Results, replay and photo finish

Before

After

After: REPLAY

  • FThe highlight clip was a file name on a line.
  • 13Line camera (a photo finish): a camera on the painted line records one column of pixels per frame, so across the strip is time, and each runner appears at the moment their body crossed the line. A coloured tick marks the first three across, with the gap. An open question it surfaced: the start grid is staggered forward of the line and every runner is timed over the full distance from their own spot, so the back rows finish a few metres past the painted line. The order at the line can therefore differ from the official result, and the caption says "first across" rather than "winner". Moving everyone's finish onto the line is a race-rules decision, so it is left for you.
  • 14AGAIN, REPLAY and FIELD (plus NEXT in a season) as icons over one word.
  • 15The clip loops behind the card the whole time; REPLAY takes the card away to watch it, and a tap brings the card back. (In these pictures the clip starts at the countdown only because the race was fast-forwarded to take them; in play it is the last six seconds.)

All ten UI items and the ten graphics and sound items are listed with their files and status in DOCS/README.md, section "Graphics, sound and one-screen UI pass".
